title: Over 25% of the Stocks in the S&P 500 Are Down 40% or More. 4 Bargain Tech Stocks to Buy Now
author: Geoffrey Seiler
description: With over 25% of S&P 500 stocks down 40% or more from their highs, the article identifies four undervalued tech stocks as bargain opportunities: Netflix benefits from recession-resistant streaming and advertising growth; Oracle offers leveraged exposure to cloud computing with a massive backlog; ServiceNow is well-positioned for agentic AI orchestration; and AppLovin trades at a cheap valuation with strong revenue and earnings growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock is down significantly but company shows recession-resistant business model, strong advertising growth potential, pricing power, and attractive forward P/E of 18.5x with continued subscriber growth opportunities.

Major growth in cloud computing infrastructure with $664 billion backlog; beaten-down stock price offers upside potential despite high leverage and cash burn concerns; strong cloud computing economics with quick paybacks.

title: Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which AI Software Stock Has the Edge?
author: Na
description: Salesforce and ServiceNow are both expanding their AI capabilities, but Salesforce emerges as the more attractive investment. Salesforce's Agentforce ARR surged 240% YoY to $1.5B with rising earnings estimates, while trading at a forward P/E of 14.76 versus ServiceNow's 28.99. ServiceNow shows strong AI adoption but faces margin pressure from higher infrastructure costs and acquisition-related financial risks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Rapid AI growth with Agentforce ARR up 240% YoY to $1.5B, upward earnings estimate revisions (18% increase over 60 days), lower forward P/E valuation of 14.76, and successful conversion of large customer base to AI products.

Strong AI ACV growth exceeding $1B with 40% sequential acceleration and 9x increase in Agentic AI production customers, but offset by declining gross margins (78% vs 81% YoY), higher AI infrastructure costs, flat earnings estimates over 60 days, and elevated valuation at 28.99 forward P/E with acquisition-related financial risks.

title: UiPath Stock Gains 33% in 6 Months: Should You Buy, Hold or Fold?
author: Na
description: UiPath (PATH) has gained 33% over six months, driven by expanding AI capabilities through its Maestro platform and improving profitability. Q2 revenues rose 13% to $410M with ARR climbing 12% to $1.94B. Trading at a forward P/E of 15.29 versus the industry average of 30.92, PATH appears undervalued. However, intensifying competition and uncertain enterprise spending pose risks to growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 33% six-month performance, 13% revenue growth, 12% ARR growth, fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability, healthy balance sheet with $1.4B cash, expanding AI adoption (18 of 20 largest deals incorporated AI), and attractive forward P/E of 15.29 versus industry 30.92. Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating supports positive outlook.

Positioned as an industry peer with established customer relationships and expanding AI capabilities in enterprise workflow automation. However, rising competition and continued investment requirements could pressure profitability, creating a balanced risk-reward profile.

Relevant industry peer offering exposure to intelligent automation and enterprise software modernization. Benefits from digital transformation demand but faces competitive pressures and enterprise budget fluctuations that could affect growth prospects.

title: Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Jake Lerch
description: Salesforce and ServiceNow represent a classic growth-versus-value investment choice in enterprise software. Salesforce offers superior profitability (21.5% operating margin), lower valuation (13.4x forward P/E), and strong free cash flow, while ServiceNow delivers faster revenue growth (20.9% YoY) and AI-driven momentum but trades at a premium valuation (33.9x forward P/E). The article concludes Salesforce has distinct advantages in profitability and valuation for 2026.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong profitability with 18% net margin and 21.5% operating margin, lower valuation at 13.4x forward P/E, robust free cash flow of $14.4B, well-diversified customer base, and improved operational efficiency. Article concludes it has distinct advantages in profitability and valuation.

Delivers superior revenue growth at 20.9% YoY, strong AI-powered platform momentum, strategic partnerships with Nvidia and Microsoft, and serves 8,700 enterprise customers including 600+ high-value clients. However, higher valuation at 33.9x forward P/E and lower profitability margins limit its relative attractiveness.

title: Here's Where Palantir and 4 Other AI Software Stocks Could Be in 5 Years
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: The article analyzes five AI software stocks divided into two camps: those proving AI revenue (Palantir, CrowdStrike) trading at steep valuations with limited room for error, and those offering faster growth at lower multiples (SoundHound, AppLovin, ServiceNow). Each company presents different risk-reward profiles over the next five years, with concerns ranging from valuation sustainability to market dependency.
